object.text: The entorhinal cortex contains grid cells that discharge in a striking geometric sequence. As an individual moves through a space, these neurons trigger at various points to form a precise hexagonal lattice, effectively overlaying the surroundings with a hidden grid. This internal navigation system, which allows the brain to calculate direction and distance independently of external cues, was identified by Nobel laureates May-Britt and Edvard Moser in 2014. Remarkably, this hexagonal code will extend beyond physical space, mapping abstract concepts and memories too.
